$comment: Canonical machine-readable typography definition for apps/web. Normative source: apps/web/src/styles/TYPOGRAPHY.md (this file encodes that spec; the spec's prose stays the rationale). NOT yet a generator input: no CSS, Tailwind utility, or component reads this file — index.css + tokens.css are still the runtime source. Every size and line-height is explicit here; nothing is inherited from framework defaults.

sans.name: Geist Variable
sans.description: The only proportional face: interface text and reading text. Emphasis inside a sentence changes weight, never family.

mono.name: JetBrains Mono Variable
mono.description: Code and technical content ONLY: terminal, editor, code blocks, tool output, diff code and the diff header path, inline code, shell commands, slash-command syntax, keycaps. Never identity or label text.

accent.name: Brand display (currently Geist Variable)
accent.description: Brand display role, kept as a named alias so a licensed display face can be dropped in at this one line. Cabinet Grotesk previously named here and has been RETIRED (it was never loaded); do not restore it.

xs.description: The single compact proportional size: dense metadata, captions, helper text, status chrome, eyebrows. No 11px or 9px proportional tier exists.

sm.description: THE default UI text: nav, trees, lists, dialogs, settings, buttons, forms, labels.

body.description: The base body size; also the long-form inline-code size (text-base-mono). --font-base is its alias and feeds the spacing scale.

md.description: Reading text AND the heading size — one value, two semantic roles (text-base vs text-md).

lg.description: Large display: the header wordmark, and the OTP code exception.

mono.description: The dense technical (mono) tier; also the size Monaco and xterm read.

default.description: The global line-height AND the declared line-height of every size tier — never a framework default.

tight.description: The brand hero, the header scope block, rail rows, prose h1/h2.

normal.description: Prose code blocks (denser than the prose body).

prose.description: The markdown prose root. The one line-height with no CSS token behind it yet.

brand.description: Lives inside the brand role only.

regular.description: ALL body/UI text, including entity names, list items, eyebrows, status labels, and active nav/tab states — active is expressed as COLOUR, never weight.

medium.description: Buttons; in-page panel/section headings; settings sub-headings; compact (toast/confirm) titles; inline sentence emphasis; markdown <strong>.

semibold.description: Dialog titles; Welcome card titles; markdown h1-h6 and table th; alert titles; ask_user_question card titles.

roles.name: Brand heading

fontSize.note: The brand role carries family/weight/tracking only; each usage sets its own size + line-height. Both usages are enumerated in `variants`.

roles.description: The canonical ThinkRail brand display style. No other composed accent-font treatment may exist.
usages: Welcome hero (the shown project's name or PRODUCT_NAME)

roles.name: Dialog title
roles.description: The title of a modal surface.
usages: AskUserQuestionCard question title and 'Review your answers' (dialog-title analogs)

roles.name: Card title
roles.description: The dialog-title WEIGHT at the card's own smaller size — matching the weight is what makes a card read as a title.

roles.name: Panel / section title
roles.description: An in-page heading (600 is modal, 500 is in-page).
usages: Settings section h3s: AppearanceSettings, ProvidersSettings, GithubSettings, PrivacySettings, TemplatesSettings

roles.name: Compact title
roles.description: The title of a transient or dense surface.

roles.name: Entity name
roles.description: The name of a project, workspace, skill, template, model, spec or file. Proportional — never mono. Active/selected state is a colour change, not a weight change.

usages: ProjectTree workspace row (name over branch sub-line)

roles.name: Entity screen heading
roles.description: An entity name promoted to a screen's primary heading — the only place an entity name grows.

roles.name: Supporting text (page)
roles.description: Page-level supporting copy — the reading tier, never a UI control.

roles.name: Reading text
roles.description: Long-form text the user reads rather than operates: chat messages. Markdown bodies use the prose group.

roles.name: UI text
roles.description: The default interface text: menu and list items, tree rows, form fields, tabs, nav. Buttons are this size at weight 500.

roles.name: Metadata
roles.description: Timestamps, counts, ids, paths, branches and refs. A branch is metadata on EVERY surface — header line, rail sub-line and empty-workspace screen are all proportional.

roles.name: Helper text
roles.description: Explanatory text under a control, and placeholders (placeholder:text-hint). Same metrics as metadata, different semantic role.

roles.name: Neutral status label
roles.description: Plain secondary text in sentence case — no uppercase, no tracking, no weight bump.

roles.name: Empty state
roles.description: The 'nothing here' line inside a panel. Tool cards add italic for absent output.

variants.description: The projects-rail placeholder is deliberately one tier larger.
Tool cards mark absent output with italic.

roles.name: Eyebrow / section label
roles.description: THE small uppercase label that titles a group or section. Carries the whole type style; the call site adds only colour. RESERVED for eyebrow/section-label content — a pill that merely looks similar uses label-pill instead.

roles.name: Label pill
roles.description: A bordered/filled pill carrying a short status or tag word. Shares the eyebrow's metrics deliberately, but NOT its semantic role — a pill is not a section label, so it spells its own classes.

roles.name: Mono / code text
roles.description: The dense technical tier: terminal, editor, tool output, diff code and the diff header path, shell commands, slash-command syntax, keycaps. Monaco and xterm read the same size + family so third-party surfaces match.
usages: TerminalInstance (xterm: size and family read from the same tokens)
monacoSetup sharedEditorOptions (all editors and both diff panes)
NewWorkspaceDialog '/' hint and the return keycap

variants.description: Tool output loosens the line-height for scanability.

roles.name: Inline code
roles.description: Code inside a sentence of long-form (reading-tier) content — one tier below the prose body so it sits level with it. Inline code inside 12px UI sentences uses mono-code-text instead.

roles.name: Code block
roles.description: A fixed-size code block in UI chrome (on bg-elevated / bg-bg-dark). Markdown's fenced blocks are em-relative instead — see prose-code-block and the exceptions list.

roles.name: Prose body
roles.description: The root of every rendered markdown document, and the basis all relative prose sizes resolve against. ONE prose group serves both markdown surfaces — there is no separate chat vs spec markdown system.

roles.name: Prose strong
roles.description: Inline emphasis inside prose. Both skins declare it explicitly to beat preflight; emphasis is a weight change, never a family change.

roles.name: Prose h1
roles.description: Document title. Relative to the prose body on purpose: a document's internal hierarchy scales with its root, which a fixed px scale cannot express.

roles.name: Prose h2
roles.description: Section heading.

roles.name: Prose h3
roles.description: Sub-section heading.

roles.name: Prose h4
roles.description: Body-sized heading: hierarchy from weight and spacing, not size.

roles.name: Prose h5
roles.description: Below-body heading.

roles.name: Prose h6
roles.description: The smallest heading; rendered in the muted colour.

roles.name: Prose inline code
roles.description: Code inside a prose sentence — the same metrics as the inline-code role, named here so the prose group is complete. Fixed (not relative) so it sits level with the prose body.

roles.name: Prose code block
roles.description: A fenced block inside a document: em-relative so it scales with the prose skin, deliberately NOT the fixed mono tier. Shiki-highlighted blocks carry the same size.

roles.name: Prose blockquote
roles.description: Body metrics in the muted colour with an accent rule — deliberately NOT italic, since quotes can be long.

roles.name: Prose list
roles.description: List items carry body typography; only indent and item spacing differ between the two skins.

roles.name: Prose table header
roles.description: A GFM table header cell. The 0.9em comes from the table root, which sets the size for header and body cells alike; the header adds weight only.

exceptions.name: Welcome hero size
exceptions.reason: The brand role carries no size by design, so each brand usage sets its own. 44px exists only here.

exceptions.name: Login OTP code
exceptions.reason: Intentional emphasis: a code the user must read aloud or copy accurately. The only mono usage at 18px and the only use of the widest tracking.

exceptions.name: Markdown relative scale

style.note: Factors live on the prose-* roles: 2 / 1.5 / 1.25 / 1 / 0.875 / 0.85 for h1-h6, 0.85 for fenced code, 0.9 for tables.

exceptions.reason: A rendered document needs an internally proportional scale that tracks its root; a fixed-px token scale cannot express that. This is the system's only relative sizing.

exceptions.name: Prose root line-height
exceptions.reason: 1.65 reads better in long documents than the global 1.6. It is the one line-height value with no CSS token behind it yet — a token would let the two stop drifting.
exceptions.openQuestion: Give it a token (e.g. --line-height-prose) or fold it into the global 1.6.

exceptions.name: Mono inside 12px UI sentences
exceptions.reason: Command syntax and code-editing surfaces stay mono even inside UI text: slash-command names, the ExtUiDialog JSON editor, gh commands, the new-workspace '/' hint, the diff header path, the return keycap. Mono here marks CODE, never an identity or label.

exceptions.name: Per-usage line-height overrides

style.note: leading-none (dialog/card titles), leading-tight (hero, header scope block, rail rows, prose h1/h2), leading-snug (card subtitles, prose h3), leading-relaxed (tool output), 1.65 (prose root).

exceptions.reason: A tier's declared line-height is the default, not a ceiling: a `leading-*` utility sets --tw-leading and wins. Each override is enumerated so none is accidental.

exceptions.name: Remaining 500 weights
exceptions.reason: NOT sanctioned — out of scope for the typography pass and left for the entity-consistency pass: form-field labels (TemplateEditorDialog), the privacy toggle row label, the chat plan strip label, and the completed-todo group title (where 500 marks a done row).

exceptions.name: Unused scale tokens

style.note: --font-lg2 (20px), --font-xl (25px), --font-xxl (40px), --compact-font-base (9px), --uppercase-size/-weight/-spacing exist in tokens.css but no role uses them; --compact-font-base is written on every boot by utils/fontScale.ts with no reader.

exceptions.reason: Deliberately left in place, and deliberately absent from this file: a role-driven definition should not carry sizes no role claims.
